arjun_s: Heads-up: seeing p99 tail spikes (~2.1s) on low-latency lanes over the last 2 hours. Traces point to a pattern: very long prompts + repeated external tool calls + lots of KV cache reloads. Rolling up data now.

maya_r: Can you paste an example trace?

arjun_s: Example (anonymized):
```
request_id: rq_1a2b3c
seq_len: 340
microbatch_size: 2
kernel_path: small_seq_attn -> fused_gemm -> kv_write
generated_tokens: 180
tool_calls: 3 (external_http)
observed_latency: 2.18s (p99)
```

samuel: Tool-calls plus long context is a classic: we may be holding GPU shards open while waiting on external I/O, causing KV pages to be evicted and reloaded when the request resumes. Disk->GPU page loads are expensive.

elaine: We saw a Europe incident like this last month. The KV eviction threshold was hit because the page residency heuristic assumed short-lived requests. When a long request returns after an external call, it tries to restore big KV pages -> ~400-600ms penalty.

arjun_s: Profiler summary from affected pod:
```
cpu_wait: 120ms
gpu_compute: 1.1s
kv_page_load_disk_to_gpu: 480ms
kernel_switch_overhead: 60ms
batch_padding_cost: 90ms
```

maya_r: Notice kernel_switch_overhead spikes when sequence-length variance in a microbatch is high. Our current kernel selection heuristic picks for the median sequence length to favor throughput, which is biting us here: median(seq)=40 but max(seq)=340 so we end up using small-seq kernels for a long request. That causes repeated rematerialization and KV churn.

samuel: Is the kernel pick done per-microbatch or per-request? I thought we picked per-microbatch using median. If so, a single long req in a microbatch of 2 is problematic.

arjun_s: Correct, pick is per-microbatch using median(seq_lengths). This optimizes p50/p95 but hurts p99 outliers.

elaine: Two axes of mitigation: 1) routing/serving lane for suspected long contexts (microbatch=1, reserved pool) and 2) smarter kernel pick: use max or a predicted final length to decide.

maya_r: Proposed experiments:
- set microbatch_size=1 on canary pods for routes flagged for long prompts (expect p99 drop, throughput loss)
- change kernel-pick: if max_seq > 256 then use long-seq kernels for entire microbatch
- implement KV pin-on-toolcall: mark requests with pending external calls so their KV pages are excluded from eviction for a short window

samuel: Also add an escape hatch: if an external tool call has been pending >200ms, mark the request pinned. That should cut eviction churn during slow external waits.

arjun_s: Ran a quick canary with microbatch=1 on a tiny pod. Results: p99 dropped 2.18s -> 1.02s, p50 rose ~5%. Kernel-switch events dropped ~75%, KV page loads reduced ~60%.

maya_r: Good signal but can't flip microbatch=1 cluster-wide. We should consider dynamic routing: use a length-predictor model (prompt metadata + initial tokens) to estimate final length and pick lane accordingly.

elaine: I can prototype a per-request kernel pin using a simple length predictor (trained on prompt templates + user metadata). If predicted_final_len > 256, pin long-seq kernel for the request even if batch median is small.

samuel: Action list:
- arjun_s: add detailed logging for kernel picks (heuristic used, median vs max vs predicted) and KV pin events
- maya_r: implement KV pin-on-toolcall flag in runtime and make eviction policy consult it
- elaine: prototype length-predictor + per-request kernel pinning
- infra-bot: schedule canary: 2 pods with microbatch=1 and kernel-pin-threshold=256

infra-bot: Canary scheduled -> id c-180765-01 on prod-sim cluster. Metrics will be posted to #eng-runtime-canaries.

arjun_s: Also flagged embedding-cache pressure: long contexts often compute extra embeddings which evict other embeddings and add I/O. Please monitor embedding cache hit rates.

maya_r: If canary looks good we'll gate kernel-pick changes behind a feature flag and A/B on 10% traffic. Keep an eye on throughput and cost per token metrics.

elaine: If kernel-pin + KV-pin reduce p99 without too much throughput loss, we can apply the heuristic selectively to routes by traffic profile.

samuel: Queueing follow-ups: KERNEL-542 (kernel pick logs + policy), KV-438 (pin on toolcall), ROUTE-77 (dynamic lane routing). Reconvene after 30m canary window. :eyes:
